analysis.title: Record Nasdaq Longs Walk Into Megacap Earnings Week: Goldman Warns "Meaningful Futures Selling Could Ensue"
key_insights: Nasdaq non-dealer net futures positioning hit a new nominal high in the week through Oct 20. Non-dealers bought $9.5B of futures while the index fell 3.5%, the third straight week of buying and $21.8B cumulative since Sep 29 (CFTC data).
Goldman futures trader Robert Quinn says length remains elevated heading into more megacap tech results. If Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet fail to impress, meaningful futures selling could ensue.
MSFT and GOOGL report Wednesday after the close and AMZN reports Thursday. The FOMC decision is also Wednesday.
On Oct 22 Meta fell 7.0% after its Q3 print and a forecast of a significant spending increase. Hyperscalers fell 4.1%, Memory 8.6% and Semis 6.5%. Meta CDS widened to a record.

Nasdaq fell 2.9% on Oct 22 and futures aggregate open interest rose $10.6B, the largest one-day increase of 2026 excluding roll periods. Rising OI with a falling price and weak funding points to sizeable new shorts.

From Oct 22 through 26 Nasdaq recovered 1.1% and futures OI fell back $9B. Meta rose Monday after announcing a ~$95B equity raise (~$35B immediate underwritten offerings plus a ~$60B at-the-market program).

Funding cheapened on both an outright and relative basis, so longs were also cutting, not only shorts covering. Nasdaq 3-month funding is ~85, down from ~88 in mid-October and above the ~50 lows of August. The Nasdaq-vs-S&P funding spread peaked near 7.5 and fell to ~4.5.

CTAs were likely a key seller. Goldman's momentum framework shows Nasdaq short-term momentum near -3.5, medium-term near 0, and long-term down from ~16 to ~8. JPMorgan notes CTA US equity exposure has fallen every day since Oct 13, led by Nasdaq.
Goldman's CTA model has trend followers selling ~$23.5B of global equities this week in a flat tape, ~$60.7B in a down tape, and buying only ~$3.6B if stocks rally, roughly a 17-to-1 asymmetry.
Hedge funds have already de-risked. Goldman Prime shows US long/short net leverage at 43.4%, the 0th percentile on a five-year lookback, and fundamental L/S net leverage at a one-year low.

JPMorgan Market Intel is Tactically Bullish, arguing a good batch of hyperscaler prints could build momentum into the post-midterm seasonal window. Its delta-one team flagged a record ~$12.7B of semiconductor ETF inflows last week. JPM concedes there has not been a complete positioning washout.
JPMorgan's international desk notes the SOX-vs-SPX drawdown now rivals 2008, which could set up a tactical AI-infrastructure bounce before year-end.

Goldman US sales trading sees two-way risk. Recent tech bounces came from a lack of heavy supply rather than real buying, and the derivatives desk is pitching short-dated QQQ call spreads to play a positioning squeeze through earnings.

Goldman's Rich Privorotsky lists four things that matter for hyperscaler earnings: capex (flat or higher is fine, a cut would hurt picks-and-shovels names), backlog conversion to revenue, free cash flow conversion in out quarters, and financing (equity vs debt). He says the cost of capital for AI has risen and credit is flashing yellow to red relative to equities.

Goldman TMT specialists (GIR) see FY28 Microsoft capex at $319B vs the Street's $252B. Amazon capex is under scrutiny amid reports of idle Nvidia racks that cannot be powered. Further equity issuance or balance-sheet strain is unlikely to be well received.
The author's view is that asymmetry runs to the downside: upside needs perfection, downside needs one more Meta. The 29K level in Nasdaq futures held on Oct 23 by roughly 100 points.
